scoring.note: Each criterion is scored 1-10 by each panel judge. Below-threshold criteria must produce a SPECIFIC diagnosis + fix (not vague judgment). Judges cite which corpus rule the artifact violates.

criteria.name: Loudness consistency across the whole piece
criteria.what_good_looks_like: Master loudness -16 LUFS ±1.5 across ALL scenes (storyteller masters at -16 LUFS / -1.5 dBTP / LRA 11). No scene jumps louder/quieter than ±1.5 LU from the master. True peak never exceeds -1.0 dBTP (no clipping).
criteria.evidence_required: ffprobe/ffmpeg loudness measurement per scene; gate_loudness.py output; no clipping in waveform.
criteria.poor: Scenes vary >2 LU from master; peaks near 0 dBTP; inconsistent perceived volume scene-to-scene.
criteria.great: Rock-steady -16 LUFS across every scene; effortless listen; no level rides needed.

criteria.name: Spectral / EQ balance (speech intelligibility)
criteria.what_good_looks_like: Energy in the 1-4 kHz intelligibility band 24-44% (narration) or 24-49% (drama); mud (bass+low-mid 60-500 Hz) 16-36% (narration) / 18-47% (drama); spectral centroid ~2000-2900 Hz. Not dull (<500 Hz centroid) or harsh/brittle (>4000 Hz). No excessive sibilance.
criteria.evidence_required: gate_eq.py spectral bands output; spectral centroid; sibilance measurement.
criteria.poor: All energy in bass/low-mid (mud), almost none in 1-4 kHz intelligibility; centroid far from human speech; harsh sibilance.
criteria.great: Clear, present, natural speech spectrum; balanced lows; no listener fatigue.

criteria.name: Reverb / acoustic-space consistency
criteria.what_good_looks_like: All sounds in a scene share similar reverb characteristics (the corpus rule: if dialogue sounds like a cathedral but footsteps are dry, listeners notice). Room preset matches the scene's stated [SPATIAL: room] cue. Reverb per-character is consistent with their cast-block reverb field.
criteria.evidence_required: Reverb preset per scene matches script [SPATIAL:] cue; no scene where elements clash acoustically.
criteria.poor: Dialogue in a hall but SFX dry; reverb changes mid-scene without a spatial cue justifying it; characters in the same scene sound in different rooms.
criteria.great: Every element sits in the same believable acoustic space; the room sells the scene; spatial cues are honored.

criteria.name: Spatial placement / stereo field (when spatial cues used)
criteria.what_good_likes_like: Characters placed per their cast-block position (center/L/R); pan cues (e.g. [SPATIAL: pan L→R]) executed with the stated duration; narrator anchored center; movement reads naturally. Spatial audio serves the story (BBC rule: don't use spatial for its own sake).
criteria.evidence_required: Script spatial cues present; rendered audio honors them (pan/placement audible); movement cues timed.
criteria.poor: All voices dead-center regardless of scripted positions; pan cues ignored; spatial placement contradicts the blocking.
criteria.great: The stereo/3D field tells part of the story — you know where each character stands; movement is motivated and clear.

criteria.name: Music/SFX beds sit under dialogue (ducking + level)
criteria.what_good_looks_like: ATMOS/MUSIC beds duck under dialogue per their [ATMOS: ... duck: N] gain; dialogue always intelligible over beds; beds audible but never competing. No 'wall of sound' burying the voice.
criteria.evidence_required: Beds duck when dialogue present; dialogue remains intelligible; gain values match script cues.
criteria.poor: Music or ambience overwhelms dialogue; ducking absent; listener strains to hear the voice.
criteria.great: Beds support the emotion and sit perfectly beneath the voice; you feel them but never fight them.

criteria.name: Dynamic range + noise floor
criteria.what_good_looks_like: LRA ~11 (storyteller target); no hiss/room-tone noise audible in silences; no pumping/breathing artifacts; silences are clean (gate_ambience passes); no clipped transients.
criteria.evidence_required: gate_ambience.py output; LRA measurement; noise floor check in pauses; no clipping in transients.
criteria.poor: Audible hiss in pauses; room tone inconsistent; breathing/mouth noise; overly compressed (no dynamics) or wildly dynamic.
criteria.great: Clean, quiet floor; dynamics serve the emotion; pauses are restful not noisy.

criteria.name: Voice pacing + pause placement (per voice-acting corpus)
criteria.what_good_looks_like: Pauses placed per corpus: [pause: 1.0-2.0s] after rhetorical questions + paragraph boundaries; [pause: 0.5s] after punch lines; [pause: 0.8s] contrast before turns/reversals. At least one ≥0.9s scene-boundary pause; gaps NOT all identical (robotic-uniform ~0.28s = FAIL). Inter-line gap 0.42s on speaker change; narrator beats 0.55s. No run-on >25 words without a pause break.
criteria.evidence_required: silencedetect output; pause-length distribution; no uniform gaps; corpus pause constants honored.
criteria.poor: Robotic uniform pacing; no scene breaths; run-on sentences; pauses in wrong places (mid-thought).
criteria.great: Pacing breathes; pauses land where the story needs them; every scene boundary is audible; rhythm feels human and intentional.

criteria.name: Emotive delivery + character voice consistency
criteria.what_good_looks_like: Character voices match cast-block descriptors + emotion cues (angry/weary/etc. map to vocal params); same character sounds like the same voice across scenes; emotion reads in the delivery, not just the words; narrator is stable and distinct from characters.
criteria.evidence_required: Cast-block voice descriptors honored; character consistency across episodes/scenes; emotion cues audible.
criteria.poor: Character voice drifts between scenes; emotion cues ignored (reads flat); two characters sound identical; narrator collides with a character voice.
criteria.great: Each character is instantly recognizable and consistent; emotion lands; the cast feels cast.

criteria.name: Story clarity — can a listener follow it?
criteria.what_good_looks_like: A first-time listener can tell who is speaking, where they are, and what is happening — from the mix alone. Scene changes are audible. The spatial/reverb/music choices support comprehension, not confusion.
criteria.evidence_required: A blind listen (judge listens without script) can follow scene/character/spatial changes.
criteria.poor: Confusing who spoke; scene transitions muddy; spatial choices obscure rather than clarify.
criteria.great: The mix alone tells the story — you never need the script to know where you are and who's talking.
